beats.intro: A price goes from twelve dollars to fifteen. A crowd shrinks from eighty people to sixty. [[q]]How big is the change? Percent rate of change answers that question.
beats.rule: Here's the method. [[r]]Divide the change by the original amount, and write the result as a percent. [[q]]A shirt's price goes from twelve dollars to fifteen. [[bar]]Start with the original, twelve dollars: that's one hundred percent. [[grow]]The price grows by three dollars. [[frac]]Three out of the original twelve is one quarter. [[pct]]One quarter is twenty-five percent, so the price rose twenty-five percent. [[see]]On the bar, the three-dollar piece is exactly one quarter of the original.
beats.decrease: Decreases work the same way. [[q]]A crowd shrinks from eighty people to sixty. [[bar]]The original is eighty. [[drop]]It loses twenty people. [[frac]]Twenty out of eighty is one quarter, [[pct]]so that's a twenty-five percent decrease.
beats.original: The most common mistake is dividing by the wrong number. [[q]]Always divide by the original amount, the one you started from. [[ex]]From sixty back up to eighty is a change of twenty again, [[calc]]but now the original is sixty, so the change is twenty out of sixty: one third, about thirty-three point three percent. [[same]]The same twenty people make a different percent, because the starting amount is different.
beats.trap: That leads to a surprise. [[q]]A price of one hundred dollars goes up fifty percent. [[up]]It becomes one hundred fifty. [[down]]Then it goes down fifty percent. Fifty percent of one fifty is seventy-five, [[end]]so the price ends at seventy-five dollars, not one hundred. [[why]]The decrease was a percent of a bigger number.
beats.big: Increases can be more than one hundred percent. [[q]]From six to eighteen, the change is twelve. [[calc]]Twelve out of six is two, which is two hundred percent. [[see]]The amount grew by two whole copies of itself.
beats.q2: Quick check. Find the percent change.
beats.wrap: Percent rate of change is the change divided by the original amount, written as a percent. [[w1]]If the amount goes up, it's a percent increase; if it goes down, a percent decrease. [[w2]]Always divide by where you started. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
